questions.prompt: An AP specialist at Brightfield Office Supply enters a PO-matched invoice and it comes back with a "quantity billed exceeds quantity received" hold. Based on where Payables sits in the procure-to-pay chain, what does this hold most likely mean?
options: Receiving has not yet recorded the delivery, so the quantity Payables is matching against doesn't yet reflect what actually arrived
The supplier's invoice was coded directly to an account instead of being matched to a purchase order
The business unit's primary ledger has not been assigned, so no chart of accounts exists for the invoice
The payment term assigned to the supplier has no due date calculation method configured
questions.explain: Payables sits downstream of Procurement and Receiving and reacts to whatever documents already exist upstream. A "quantity billed exceeds quantity received" hold is almost always an upstream problem, not a Payables problem: the warehouse or requester simply hasn't recorded the receipt yet, so the quantity Payables is checking against is incomplete rather than wrong.

questions.prompt: A supplier calls Brightfield asking why they haven't been paid yet. The AP specialist checks the invoice and sees: Invoice status = Validated, Approval status = Approved, Accounting status = Accounted, Payment status = Unpaid, with a due date 11 days out. What should the AP specialist tell the supplier?
options: The invoice is fully validated, approved, and accounted; it's simply not due yet, so payment is on track
The invoice is stuck on a hold and can't be paid until the hold is cleared
The invoice still hasn't cleared the approval workflow, which is blocking payment
The invoice can't be paid because it hasn't been accounted to the ledger yet
questions.explain: The four status fields move independently on purpose. An invoice can be Validated, Approved, and Accounted while still showing Unpaid simply because its due date hasn't arrived — that's a normal, healthy state, not a problem. Only the invoice status (via holds) blocks payment, and this invoice has no hold.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: Most Payables setup — Payables Options, payment terms, and more — is scoped at the level of the ________, the organizational entity that actually processes a given transaction.
questions.explain: A business unit (BU) is the organizational entity behind "who entered this invoice, and under which rules." Most Payables setup is scoped at the BU level, which is why two business units in the same company can run entirely different tolerances, default payment terms, or approval rules even while posting to the same chart of accounts.

questions.prompt: Match each of an invoice's four independent status fields to the question it actually answers.
right: Has it been accounted to the ledger — Unaccounted, Partially Accounted, or Accounted?
Has it cleared the approval workflow, if one applies — Required, Not Required, Initiated, Approved, or Rejected?
Has it been paid — Unpaid, Partially Paid, or Paid?
Has the invoice passed validation — Incomplete, Never Validated, Needs Revalidation, Validated, or Cancelled?
questions.explain: Invoice status tracks validation (Incomplete through Validated or Cancelled). Approval status tracks whether the approval workflow has cleared. Accounting status tracks whether the invoice has posted to the ledger. Payment status tracks whether it's been paid. Oracle Fusion keeps these four separate because each answers a different question about the same invoice, and they move mostly independently of each other.

questions.prompt: Put these stages of the procure-to-pay chain, as described in Lesson 1, in the correct order, from an employee's initial request through to the supplier being paid.
items: Requisition — an employee requests to buy something through Self Service Procurement
Purchase order — Procurement turns the approved requisition into a legal commitment to a supplier
Receipt — the warehouse or requester confirms the goods or services actually arrived
Invoice — the supplier bills for what was ordered and delivered, and Payables takes over
Payment — the invoice is paid through the Payments module, using a bank account and a payment method
questions.explain: The procure-to-pay chain runs requisition to purchase order to receipt to invoice to payment: an employee requests the purchase, Procurement commits to a supplier via a PO, Receiving confirms delivery, Payables records and validates the resulting invoice, and finally Payments settles it. Payables only takes over once the invoice arrives — it doesn't own the three steps before it.

questions.prompt: In the Oracle Fusion supplier hierarchy, what is a supplier site?
options: A specific location or business arrangement with a supplier, carrying an address plus operational controls like payment terms and whether it's a purchasing site, a pay site, or both
A person at the supplier organization that Brightfield's buyers or AP team can contact
The top-level party record carrying the supplier's name, tax registration details, and overall status
A certified attribute of the supplier, such as Woman Owned or Veteran Owned, tracked for compliance purposes
The business relationship value that determines whether a supplier can be paid
The profile tab where a supplier's bank account is attached
questions.explain: A supplier site represents a specific location or business arrangement with a supplier, carrying an address and operational controls such as payment terms, tax details, and whether it functions as a purchasing site, a pay site, or both. A single supplier can have multiple sites, each needing its own active business-unit assignment to be transacted against.
questions.distractorExplain: Option C describes the supplier itself, not a site. The supplier is the top-level party record holding information true regardless of location — name, tax registration, overall status — while the site is the lower-level record tied to a specific address and set of transactional controls. Confusing the two is exactly the mistake the guide warns against.

questions.prompt: Brightfield's AP team enters an invoice against a newly created supplier site. The site has a complete address and payment terms, but no one has yet assigned it to a business unit. What happens?
options: The invoice can still be entered and even approved, but the transaction can't actually be processed because the site has no active assignment to transact against
Fusion automatically creates a default business-unit assignment the first time an invoice references the site
The invoice can be entered normally, since business-unit assignment only affects purchase orders, not invoices
The supplier record is automatically reverted from Spend Authorized back to Prospective until an assignment is added
questions.explain: A site only becomes usable for transactions once it has an active site assignment to a business unit — the assignment is what actually lets a business unit create purchase orders or enter invoices against the site, and it's also where the sold-to business unit is defined. No active assignment means no transactions, even if the site itself looks perfectly complete.

questions.prompt: Select every statement below that correctly describes supplier addresses and business classifications, per the guides.
options: The Address Name is an internal label chosen by the user, not the physical street address itself
A single address can carry multiple purpose flags, such as being valid for ordering and also serving as the remit-to address
A business classification like Woman Owned or Veteran Owned is a self-reported checkbox with no certifying agency required
Each business classification carries certification details including a certificate number, a certifying agency, and an expiration date
Fusion surfaces an alert when a classification certificate has already expired or is coming up on expiration, commonly within a 30-day window
questions.explain: Address Name is a chosen internal identifier separate from the actual street address, and one address can serve several purposes (ordering, RFQ, remit-to) at once. A business classification is not a self-reported checkbox — it reflects a real, verifiable certificate with a certificate number, a certifying agency, and an expiration date, and Fusion alerts on certificates that are expired or nearing expiration, commonly within a 30-day window on either side.

questions.prompt: Select every statement below that correctly describes supplier bank accounts and payment requirements, per the guides.
options: A domestic check payment requires a bank and branch on the supplier's account, just like an international electronic payment
An international electronic payment requires a specific bank and branch identified on the account, not just an account number
If a bank account is missing or incomplete, an invoice can still validate and get approved, with the failure only showing up later at the payment step
Fusion displays the full stored bank account number to any AP staff member by default, since masking only applies to credit card numbers
A profile option controls masking of the stored account number, commonly showing only the last four digits
questions.explain: International electronic payments need a specific bank and branch identified, while a domestic check doesn't require any bank or branch detail at all — it's simply printed and mailed, which rules out the first option. A missing or incomplete bank account doesn't block invoice validation or approval; it only surfaces as a failure later, at the payment step. A masking profile option commonly shows only the last four digits of the stored account number by default, which also rules out the claim that the full number displays to any AP staff member.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a brand-new vendor often starts life with the business relationship "________" while procurement vets them, allowing participation in sourcing activity but no ability to be paid, and is later flipped to "Spend Authorized" once they clear qualification.
questions.explain: Prospective is the business relationship that lets a supplier participate in sourcing activity, such as responding to negotiations or going through qualification, but it does not yet allow the supplier to be paid. Only Spend Authorized clears a supplier for actual transactions like purchase orders and invoices.

questions.prompt: Match each supplier concept to what it actually describes, per the guides.
right: Consolidates one supplier or site into another, moving transaction references, and is treated as irreversible once completed
The standard way to retire a record no longer in use while keeping transaction history intact and reportable
Lets a prospective trading partner submit their own company details, tax ID, addresses, and banking information directly, entering a restricted-access state until Brightfield reviews it
A formal screening layer that distributes a survey, scores responses against predefined criteria, and decides whether a registering supplier is accepted
questions.explain: Registration is the self-service front door where a prospective supplier submits its own information and sits in a restricted-access state pending review. Qualification Management is the optional screening layer on top of that — survey, scoring, documentation — deciding whether to accept the registration. Inactivating retires a supplier, site, or bank account no longer in use while preserving transaction history for reporting. A merge consolidates duplicate supplier records or sites, moving transaction references onto the surviving record, and cannot be undone once it completes.

questions.prompt: Solara Packaging Co. sends Brightfield a single document that bills $5,000 for a new shipment and, on that very same statement, credits $300 for a prior short shipment. Which invoice type should this document be entered as?
options: Standard
Credit memo
Mixed
Debit memo
questions.explain: A mixed invoice combines both positive and negative line items on one document — effectively a standard invoice and a credit memo rolled into one. That is exactly this case: a new $5,000 shipment charge and a $300 credit for a prior short shipment on the same statement, so one mixed invoice records both lines instead of requiring two separate documents to be reconciled against each other.

questions.prompt: A Payables user is entering a standard invoice header for Vantree Industrial Parts. Select every statement below that is true about standard invoice headers, per the lesson.
options: The invoice number is whatever number the supplier printed on their own bill, not an internally generated Brightfield sequence
Payment terms default in from the supplier site, but can still be overridden on an individual invoice
Business unit determines which ledger and setup the invoice belongs to
Payables automatically generates a new invoice number for every invoice entered
Once payment terms default in from the site, they are locked and cannot be changed on that invoice
questions.explain: The invoice number is the supplier's own number, not a Brightfield-generated sequence — typing it accurately is what makes duplicate-invoice detection work. Payment terms and address information default from the supplier site to save data entry, but those defaults can be overridden per invoice, such as a one-time Net 15 arrangement instead of the site's usual Net 30. Business unit determines which ledger and setup the invoice belongs to. Payables does not generate the invoice number itself, and site defaults are overridable, not locked.

questions.prompt: Brightfield's invoice INV-4471 has an Item line for $3,800.00 and a Freight line for $200.00, allocated using Allocate All Lines. Select every true statement about invoice lines and distributions, per the lesson.
options: Freight and miscellaneous charges can be allocated proportionally across existing item lines using Allocate All Lines
A single invoice line can produce more than one distribution, such as when a cost is split between two departments
The sum of all of an invoice's distributions must equal the invoice's total line amount
Distribution types are unrelated to invoice line types and bear no connection between the two
Tax lines on an invoice can only ever be entered manually; Payables never generates them automatically
questions.explain: Allocate All Lines spreads a freight or miscellaneous charge proportionally across item lines, using the same account combinations those item lines already use. One line can produce several distributions, such as a 60/40 split between two departments' accounts. The sum of all distributions must tie back to the invoice's line total, which validation enforces. Distribution types actually mirror line types (Item, Freight, Miscellaneous) rather than being unrelated, and tax lines can be generated automatically or entered manually.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: in a Full distribution set, the percentages assigned across all of its lines must add up to exactly ________%.
questions.explain: A Full distribution set specifies both the accounts and the percentage of the invoice amount each one receives, and the defining rule is that those percentages across all lines in the set must total exactly 100%, as in the 70/30 Monthly Rent Split example.

questions.prompt: Match each term from the invoice import and tax lessons to what it actually is.
right: A piece of invoice information, like the ship-to location, that the tax engine uses to decide which tax applies and at what rate
Tax that the purchaser owes directly to the tax authority, which does not change the invoice's total amount to the supplier
The staging area where imported invoice data lands before it becomes a real Payables invoice
The scheduled process that reads staged rows and builds real invoices and invoice lines from them
questions.explain: Open interface tables are the staging area where imported data lands first. The Import Payables Invoices process is the scheduled step that turns valid staged rows into real invoices and lines. A tax determinant, like ship-to location, is what the Oracle Fusion Tax engine uses to pick the applicable tax and rate. Self-assessed tax is owed by the purchaser rather than the supplier, and never changes what the supplier is actually paid.

questions.prompt: Put these steps of the invoice import process, per the lesson, in the correct order.
items: A spreadsheet loader, EDI feed, scanning tool, or supplier portal writes invoice data into the open interface tables
The Import Payables Invoices process is run against the staged rows
Valid staged rows are built into real Payables invoices and invoice lines
A rejections report lists which staged rows failed, and why
The underlying data is corrected and the rejected rows are re-attempted
questions.explain: Imported data always lands in the open interface tables first, regardless of its source. Running the Import Payables Invoices process is a deliberate, scheduled step that then reads those staged rows. Rows that resolve cleanly become real invoices and lines, while every run also produces a rejections report listing what failed and why — a step that still needs the underlying issue fixed and the rows re-attempted, or those supplier invoices simply vanish from view instead of getting paid.

questions.prompt: In Oracle Fusion Payables, what does an invoice's Invoice Status field reaching "Validated" actually certify?
options: That the invoice has been approved by every required approver in the workflow
That the invoice has been paid in full to the supplier
That distributions are generated, tax and withholding are calculated, matching variances fall within tolerance, the GL period is open, currency data is sound, and no unresolved holds remain
That the invoice has passed a basic check for typos and formatting errors
That sufficient budget has been reserved under budgetary control, independent of any other checks
That the invoice has been routed to the BPM Worklist application for human review
questions.explain: Validation is one combined pass that generates and checks distributions, calculates tax and withholding, checks matching variances, GL period status, and currency conversion data, and applies or releases holds based on all of it. "Validated" status means all of that came back clean on the invoice itself — it says nothing about approval or payment, which are separate status fields.
questions.distractorExplain: Funds reservation under budgetary control is genuinely one of the things validation performs, but it's only one check among several (tax, matching, GL period, currency, and more) — it isn't what "Validated" status certifies by itself, and organizations without budgetary control enabled can still reach Validated status without any funds check happening at all.

questions.prompt: An AP specialist notices an invoice has an account hold because one of its distributions posted to an inactive GL account. She corrects the distribution to a valid, active account combination and clicks Validate again. What happens to the hold?
options: The hold remains in place until someone clicks a separate Release button, because every hold requires a deliberate manual release action regardless of what caused it
The hold clears automatically as part of revalidation, because it's an application-placed hold reacting to a condition that the Validate action re-checks
The invoice must be cancelled and re-entered from scratch, since a distribution can't be edited once a hold has been applied to it
The hold is replaced by a new matching hold, since correcting the account combination affects the invoice's match to its purchase order
questions.explain: Account holds are application-placed holds reacting to a condition the system can re-check. Once the underlying problem (the invalid account) is fixed, running Validate again re-evaluates that condition and clears the hold automatically, with no separate release click needed — exactly how the Vantree Industrial Parts account hold is resolved in the lesson's worked example.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are categories of holds described in the course material? (Select all that apply.)
options: Account holds
Matching holds
Approval holds
Funds holds
Installment holds
questions.explain: The guide groups holds into account, matching, variance, funds, installment, and supplier site categories. "Approval holds" isn't one of them — approval is tracked through a separate Approval Status field (Approved, Rejected, Not Required, etc.) that runs on an entirely different workflow engine, not through the hold mechanism validation uses.

questions.prompt: A Financial Application Administrator needs to configure Payables invoice approval rules in the BPM Worklist application. What is the name of the specific task used for this?
questions.explain: Payables invoice approval rules are configured in the BPM Worklist application, by someone in the Financial Application Administrator role, using the specific task named FinApInvoiceApproval — part of the Approval Management extensions (AMX) built on Oracle SOA Suite and Oracle Human Workflow.

questions.prompt: Brightfield's approval rule requires any non-PO invoice over $2,500 to route sequentially: first to the requesting department's manager, then to a finance reviewer. Place the steps of a $3,000 non-PO invoice from Hearthstone Logistics moving through this workflow in the correct order.
items: Invoice is validated and submitted for approval
Invoice routes to the requesting department's manager
Department manager approves the invoice
Invoice routes to the finance reviewer
Finance reviewer approves, and the invoice becomes fully approved
questions.explain: Because Brightfield's rule uses sequential routing, approvers are asked in order and the invoice doesn't move to the next approver until the current one has acted. A validated invoice first reaches the department manager; only after that approval does it advance to the finance reviewer, whose approval completes the workflow — unlike parallel routing, where both approvers would be asked at the same time.

questions.prompt: A purchase order is set up for a maintenance contract where no formal receiving step is required. The supplier invoices the exact quantity and unit price shown on the PO line. Under two-way matching, what happens?
options: The invoice is placed on a Quantity Received hold because no receipt exists
Payables validates the invoice without creating a matching hold, since two-way matching only checks quantity and price
The invoice cannot be processed at all until a receipt is logged
The invoice is automatically placed on a Price hold because no tolerance was evaluated
questions.explain: Two-way matching compares only quantity and price between the PO and the invoice — it never checks a receipt. Since both quantity and price match exactly, there's nothing for a tolerance to flag, so Payables validates the invoice without a hold, exactly as in the Cascade Industrial Parts example in Lesson 23.

questions.prompt: Select every statement below that correctly describes four-way matching, based on the chapter.
options: It adds an inspection/acceptance checkpoint on top of everything three-way matching already does
It compares quantity ordered, received, accepted, and invoiced
It replaces the need for a tolerance set, since every variance is flagged regardless of size
Organizations typically reserve it for high-value, high-risk, or regulated purchases rather than applying it to every PO
It confirms goods were inspected and meet the purchase order's requirements, not just that they arrived
questions.explain: Four-way matching builds on three-way matching (PO, receipt, invoice) by adding inspection/acceptance, comparing ordered, received, accepted, and invoiced quantities. Because it adds process overhead, organizations limit it to high-value, high-risk, or regulated purchases. Tolerance sets still apply at every matching level — four-way matching doesn't remove them, it still relies on them to decide what counts as close enough.

questions.prompt: In three-way matching, when a supplier invoices a full PO quantity but the warehouse has only logged a receipt for part of it, Payables places the invoice on what type of hold?
questions.explain: Three-way matching checks the invoiced quantity against the quantity actually logged as received, not just the quantity on the PO. When the invoice bills for more than has been received so far, Payables places a Quantity Received hold, which stays in place until the warehouse logs the remaining receipt or the invoice is corrected to match what was actually received.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the invoice type created to pay out accumulated retainage once a contract is complete and the work has been accepted?
questions.explain: Retainage is a percentage withheld from each progress payment on a contract and held back until the work is complete. Once the contract is finished and accepted, a separate retainage release invoice is created to pay out everything that was withheld across all of the contract's earlier progress invoices.

questions.prompt: Match each document or concept to its correct description.
right: An organization-issued negative-amount invoice recording a dispute before the supplier agrees
A legally required deduction remitted to a tax authority on the supplier's behalf
A supplier-issued negative-amount invoice correcting an overcharge or return
An advance payment intended to be applied against a future standard invoice from the same supplier
questions.explain: A credit memo is issued by the supplier to acknowledge an overcharge or return. A debit memo is raised internally by the organization, often while a dispute is still unresolved. A temporary prepayment is an advance meant to be applied to a later standard invoice. Withholding tax is a legally mandated deduction the organization remits to a tax authority instead of paying the supplier directly.

questions.prompt: Put these steps in the correct order for creating, paying, and applying a temporary prepayment to a standard invoice.
items: Create the prepayment invoice (type = Prepayment) for the deposit amount
Validate the prepayment invoice
Pay the prepayment in full
Receive the standard invoice for the goods or services covered by the deposit
Apply the prepayment against the standard invoice, reducing the amount still due
questions.explain: A prepayment must move through its own full lifecycle before it can do anything useful: it's created as its own invoice type, validated like any invoice, and then fully paid — an unpaid prepayment can't be applied. Only once the related standard invoice arrives can the prepayment be applied, automatically during validation or manually, reducing the net amount still owed, as shown in the BrightPath Consulting example in Lesson 26.

questions.prompt: In Oracle Fusion Payables, what does a Payment Process Profile (PPP) define?
options: The rulebook tying together the disbursement bank account, the document or file format generated, invoice grouping rules, and minimum/maximum processing limits for a payment method
The mechanism used to pay a supplier, such as check, EFT, or wire
The three-level Bank, Branch, and Account hierarchy maintained in Cash Management
The numeric ranking on an invoice used to sequence which invoices get paid first when funds are limited
The categorization used to run separate Payment Process Requests for different invoice populations, such as Employees or Trade Suppliers
The structured data file transmitted to a bank so it can process a payment automatically
questions.explain: A Payment Process Profile is the rulebook behind a payment method: it ties together the disbursement bank account funds come from, the document or file format generated, how invoices get grouped, and processing limits such as a minimum or maximum payment amount. That's why a single payment method, like EFT, can sit behind more than one PPP.
questions.distractorExplain: Option B describes a payment method, not a Payment Process Profile — the payment method is just the mechanism (check, EFT, wire), while the PPP is the deeper rulebook of bank account, file format, grouping, and limits that operates underneath that mechanism. The two are deliberately kept as separate concepts precisely because one payment method can require several different PPPs.

questions.prompt: A check was mailed to a supplier last week. The supplier calls to say it never arrived, and the organization confirms with its bank that the check has not cleared. What is the correct way to cancel this specific payment?
options: Void the payment in Payables, since it was never actually received by the supplier
Place a stop payment with the bank on that check number, mark the payment as stopped in Payables, and then reissue
Record a supplier refund for the check amount to reverse the transaction
Submit a new Payment Process Request to pay the same invoice again, leaving the original check alone
questions.explain: The check has already been issued and sent, so voiding no longer applies — void is only for a payment that hasn't left the organization's control yet. Because the check is out but hasn't cleared, a stop payment is the right tool: place the hold with the bank on that check number, mark it stopped in Payables (which returns the invoice to unpaid status), and then reissue a new payment.

questions.prompt: Which of the following situations would typically leave a supplier sitting on a credit balance that gets resolved with a Record Refund? Select all that apply.
options: An unused prepayment for an engagement that was cancelled before any invoice offset it
A credit memo larger than any invoice currently open against that supplier
A duplicate or incorrect overpayment sent to the supplier by mistake
A supplier site being restricted to only one allowed payment method
A check that was voided before it was ever mailed
questions.explain: An unused prepayment with no invoice left to offset it, a credit memo bigger than any open invoice, and an overpayment sent by mistake are the three situations the guide identifies as creating a refundable credit balance — in each case the supplier owes the organization money back with no upcoming invoice large enough to net it out. Restricting a supplier to one payment method is an unrelated setup detail, and a check voided before mailing simply returns the invoice to unpaid status rather than creating a credit balance to refund.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: a Cash Management bank account becomes eligible to be selected as the funding source for a Payment Process Profile only once it has been flagged for the ________ account use.
questions.explain: A disbursement bank account is simply a Cash Management bank account flagged for the "Payables Disbursements" account use. That flag is what makes the account eligible to be chosen as the funding source referenced by a Payment Process Profile.

questions.prompt: Match each Chapter 6 term to what it actually is.
right: The Payables action that applies a received refund against a credit memo or prepayment
A file listing every check issued in a run, which the bank checks before honoring a presented check
The mechanism used to pay a supplier: check, EFT, or wire
The rulebook defining the bank account, file format, grouping rules, and limits for a payment method
questions.explain: Payment method is the basic mechanism (check, EFT, wire); the Payment Process Profile is the deeper rulebook of bank account, format, grouping, and limits behind that mechanism; a positive pay file is the fraud-prevention list of issued checks sent ahead to the bank; and Record Refund is the Payables action used when a supplier sends money back against a credit memo or prepayment.

questions.prompt: Put these stages of a Payment Process Request in the correct order, from selection to a finished payment file.
items: Selection — scan open, validated, unpaid invoices against criteria such as pay-through date, pay group, and business unit
Build proposed payments — group selected invoices per the applicable Payment Process Profile into not-yet-final proposed payments
Review — remove an invoice, adjust a payment date, or pull a supplier out before anything is submitted
Build payments — create the actual payment records once the batch is confirmed
Format / generate payment file — produce the printable check layout or electronic payment file
questions.explain: A Payment Process Request always moves through these five stages in order: it first selects eligible invoices against defined criteria, groups them into proposed payments under the relevant Payment Process Profile, pauses for a human review step before anything is final, builds the actual payment records once confirmed, and finally formats the output — a check layout or electronic file — ready for printing or transmission.

questions.prompt: Solace Robotics runs Create Accounting in Final mode for 42 unaccounted transactions. One invoice fails because its expense account combination doesn't exist in the chart of accounts. What happens to the other 41 transactions?
options: All 42 transactions fail and no journal entries are generated until the invalid account combination is fixed
The 41 transactions account successfully; the failing invoice is skipped and reported in the error output, remaining unaccounted until the problem is fixed and the process is rerun
Oracle automatically posts the failing invoice to a default suspense account so all 42 complete together
Create Accounting automatically switches the entire batch back to Draft mode until someone corrects the account combination
questions.explain: A transaction that fails to account doesn't block the others in the batch — it's skipped and reported in the process's error output, while every other transaction accounts normally. The failed invoice stays unaccounted until the account combination is corrected and Create Accounting is run again.

questions.prompt: Which of the following are reasons an accrual (uninvoiced receipts) account balance might not clear cleanly, according to the Payables Accrual Reconciliation Report discussion?
options: A receipt was posted this period but the matching invoice isn't expected until next period
A receipt was logged with the wrong quantity and the error was never corrected
A purchase order was cancelled after goods were received and accrued, and no invoice will ever be submitted
Goods were returned to the vendor, but the original accrual entry was never reversed
The supplier's bank rejected an electronic payment file for an unrelated invoice
questions.explain: The guide lists four causes of a lingering accrual balance: normal timing gaps, uncorrected quantity mismatches, cancelled orders with no invoice coming, and return-to-vendor transactions whose original accrual was never reversed. A rejected electronic payment file is a payment-transmission problem, unrelated to the accrual account.

questions.prompt: Before closing a Payables period, the ______ report compares the ending AP liability balance in the Payables subledger against the ending AP liability balance in the General Ledger, and any non-zero difference must be explained before the period closes.
questions.explain: The Payables-to-Ledger Reconciliation report ties the subledger's AP liability balance to the GL's AP liability account. In a healthy close the two numbers match exactly; any difference points back to a transaction stuck somewhere in the accounted-transferred-posted pipeline.

questions.prompt: Match each Payables report to what it is actually used for.
right: Revalues open foreign-currency invoices and payments at a current exchange rate for reporting purposes
A detailed listing of payments issued in a period, by method and bank account
Lists outstanding, unpaid invoice balances by supplier, bucketed by how many days past due
A detailed listing of invoices entered in a given period, useful for audit and period activity review
questions.explain: The aging report buckets unpaid balances by days past due for cash planning; the Invoice Register lists invoices entered in the period for audit purposes; the Payment Register lists payments issued by method and bank account; and the Open Items Revaluation Report restates open foreign-currency balances at a current exchange rate.

questions.prompt: Put the following steps in the correct order, from finalizing accounting in Payables through to the GL balances actually being updated.
items: Create Accounting is run in Final mode, generating permanent accounting entries in the Payables subledger
The finalized entries are transferred to General Ledger as an unposted journal batch
A GL accountant reviews the batch and confirms its totals tie back to the Payables subledger
The journal batch is posted, updating the account balances in the chart of accounts
questions.explain: Accounted, transferred, and posted are three distinct states, not one event: Create Accounting (Final mode) finalizes the subledger entries, Transfer to GL moves them into GL as an unposted batch, and only posting that batch actually updates account balances — which is why reconciliation can pinpoint exactly where a mismatch occurred.

questions.prompt: Put the following steps of the Payables period close checklist in the correct order.
items: Complete invoice entry and validation for every invoice dated in the period
Resolve outstanding holds on invoices dated in the period, or deliberately carry them forward
Complete payment processing for the period, including any quick payments
Run Create Accounting in Final mode for every remaining unaccounted transaction
Reconcile Payables to GL and confirm the balances tie before closing the period
questions.explain: The close checklist runs in a fixed order because each step depends on the one before it: invoices must be entered and validated, holds resolved, and payments completed before Create Accounting can finalize everything outstanding, and only after transfer/posting is complete can the Payables-to-Ledger Reconciliation report be trusted to confirm the period is safe to close.
